summary: Gone fire lookout site on Wayne National Forest land in Perry County; no build date or staffing found, and no source describes what remains.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source describes what remains.

events.note: Entered in the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 3, 2014

evidence.supports: Site is in Perry County on Wayne National Forest land
evidence.quote: Wayne National Forest Perry County, Ohio

evidence.supports: Register added the site on September 3, 2014
Forest is public land across southeastern Ohio foothills
evidence.quote: The Wayne National Forest is a patchwork of public land that covers over a quarter million acres of Appalachian foothills of southeastern Ohio.

evidence.supports: Ohio forestry division says fire towers arose in the 1920s to suppress wildland fires
evidence.quote: According to Don Karas with the Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR), Division of Forestry, the towers arose in the 1920s from a need for wildland fire suppression.

evidence.supports: CCC built 11 steel-frame fire towers in southeast Ohio, 1933-1934
evidence.quote: In an 18-month period between 1933 and 1934, the CCC built 11 steel-frame fire towers in southeast Ohio.

evidence.supports: CCC built eight more from 1934 until disbanded in 1942
evidence.quote: They constructed another eight from 1934 until the CCC was disbanded in 1942.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone
evidence.quote: Ironpoint Perry 39.62919 -82.20756 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1560, OH 6

evidence.supports: Regional list files the site as Kehota (Ironpoint)

sources.title: Fire towers: Artifacts of our conservation past

notes_for_editor: Thin: only the register entry and the association list describe this site. No build date, design, staffing or site description was found. The CCC and state forestry sentences describe Ohio's towers in general and are context, not evidence that Ironpoint was one of them. Possible alias: the Eastern US Lookouts list files this site as KEHOTA (IRONPOINT), while the association list keeps Kehota (Maxville) as a separate site (US 1566, OH 12, 39.61974, -82.29704). A human should decide whether to add an other_name or split the record. Not written as a correction.
